Rashi on Shabbat 13a:1:1.hebrew: ואימת רבן עליהן - אין פושטין יד לשום דבר, ואפי' בחול, אלא על פי רבן:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:1:1.english: And the fear of their teacher is upon them - They do not stretch out a hand to anything, and even on a weekday, except by the instruction of their teacher.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:2:1.hebrew: פרצה - גברה, כמו: ״ופרצת ימה וקדמה״ (בראשית כח):
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:2:1.english: Spread - [It] grew strong, as in: "And you shall spread out to the west and to the east" (Genesis 28:14).

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:2:2.hebrew: שלא שנינו לא יאכל טהור עם הטמאה - מפני הערוה, לפי שלא הוצרכו לכך, שכולן אוכלין חוליהן בטהרה היו, ולא היו אוכלין עם נשותיהן טמאות:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:2:2.english: That we did not learn: "A pure [man] shall not eat with an impure [woman]" - [I.e., to prohibit this] on account of forbidden relations, because they had no need for this, as all of them were eating their non-sacred food in purity, and would not eat with their wives [when they were] impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:3:1.english: Is that to say that a zav who is a parush does not eat impure things? - For is not everything he touches impure?

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:3:2.english: They tithe - And we do not issue a decree upon a decree.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:1.hebrew: שתישן עם בעלה - במטה, כגון שהוא טמא דליכא למיחש משום טהרה, או בזמן הזה שאין בו טהרה — מי חיישי' להרגל עבירה, או דילמא כיון דאיכא היכרא מדכר דכירי:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:1.english: That she may sleep with her husband - In a bed — for example, where he is [already] ritually impure, so there is no concern on account of ritual purity; or in this era, in which there is no [practice of] ritual purity — do we suspect [that it will lead to] habituation to sin, or perhaps, since there is a reminder, they will remember?

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:2.hebrew: על השולחן - שאוכל עליו, מותר להניח בשר העוף אצל הגבינה, דקסברי בית שמאי: בשר עוף בחלב לאו דאורייתא, ולא גזרי' העלאה אטו אכילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:2.english: On the table - [A table] that one eats upon, [on which] it is permitted to place fowl meat next to cheese; for Beit Shammai hold that fowl meat with milk is not [prohibited] by Torah law, and we do not decree [against] placing [it on the table] due to [the concern of] eating [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:3.english: And it is not eaten - With it.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:4.english: And Beit Hillel say, etc. - Learn from this that it is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:5.hebrew: דליכא דיעות - שני בני אדם שיזכירו זה לזה. וה"ה נמי דמצי לשנויי דליכא שינוי להיכרא, ומיהו דעדיפא נקט — דאפי' דיעות ליכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:4:5.english: That there are not [multiple] minds - [I.e.,] two people who will remind one another. And it is likewise the case that [the Gemara] could also have answered that there is no change to serve as a reminder; however, it stated the stronger [distinction], that even [multiple] minds are not present.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:5:1.english: That they are not familiar [with each other] - So that one will not come to take from his fellow's [food] and eat [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:5:2.hebrew: אבל מכירין - אסור, ואשה ובעלה [נמי] מכירין זה את זה, וש"מ דאסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:5:2.english: However, [if] they are familiar [with each other] - [It is] forbidden; and a wife and her husband are [also] familiar with each other, and learn from this that [it is] forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:5:3.english: There is no change - For they eat in the [usual] manner of eating.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:5:4.hebrew: איכא שינוי - שאין דרך לישן אלא בקירוב בשר, כדכתיב: "שארה כסותה ועונתה", ואמר מר: "שאר" — זה קירוב בשר, שאם אמר: "אי איפשי אלא היא בבגדה והוא בבגדו" — יוציא ויתן כתובה, במס' כתובות (פ"ד דף מח.):
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:5:4.english: There is a change - For it is not the usual way to sleep except with bodily contact, as it is written: "Her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights" (Exodus 21:10), and the Master said: "She'er" — this is bodily contact; for if [the husband] said: "I do not want [to engage in marital relations] unless she is in her garment and he is in his garment," he must divorce [her] and pay the marriage contract [ketubah], in Tractate Ketubot (chapter 4, 48a).

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:8:1.hebrew: אל ההרים לא אכל - בפרק אלו הן הנשרפין בסנהדרין (דף פא.) מפרש ליה, שלא נתפרנס בזכות אבות, שלא הוצרך לכך, לפי שהוא צדיק:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:8:1.english: He did not eat upon the mountains - In the chapter “Elu Hen HaNisrafin” in Sanhedrin (81a), [the Gemara] explains it: that he did not sustain himself through the merit of the Patriarchs, for he had no need for this, because he is righteous.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:8:2.english: Just as his neighbor's wife, etc. - For seclusion is forbidden to us by Torah law, [as derived] in Kiddushin (chapter 4, 80b) from [the verse]: "Your brother, the son of your mother."

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:9:1.hebrew: ופליגא - דרב יוסף, דפשט מדרשה דהאי קרא לאיסור, אדרבי פדת:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:9:1.english: And it disagrees - [That ruling] of Rav Yosef, who resolved [the dilemma from] the exposition of this verse as a prohibition, [disagrees] with [the opinion of] Rabbi Pedat.

Rashi on Shabbat 13a:9:2.hebrew: גילוי עריות - תשמיש ממש. ושאר קורבה — ואפי' קירוב בשר — מדרבנן. והיא בבגדה, אפי' מדרבנן ליכא למגזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 13a:9:2.english: Uncovering of nakedness - [Means] actual intercourse. And other [forms of] intimacy — and even bodily contact — are [prohibited] by Rabbinic law. But [when] she is in her garment, there is no [reason] to decree even by Rabbinic law.

Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:10:1.hebrew: ופליגא דידיה אדידיה - והוא היה יודע בעצמו שלא יבא לידי הרהור, שצדיק גמור היה, כדאמרינן בפרק ב' דכתובות ('ף יז.): דרב אדא בר אהבה מרכיב לה אכתפיה ומרקד. א"ל רבנן: "אנן מהו למעבד הכי?" א"ל: "אי דמיא לכון כי כשורא — לחיי, ואי לא — לא". והספר לא חש לפרש ולהאריך כאן למה היה עושה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:10:1.english: "And his [action] contradicts his [own statement]" - And he [Ulla] knew about himself that he would not come to improper thoughts, for he was a completely righteous man, as we say in the second chapter of Ketubot (17a): that Rav Adda bar Ahavah would place her [the bride] on his shoulders and dance. The Rabbis said to him: "What is [the ruling for] us to do this?" He said to them: "If she is like a beam to you, fine; and if not, no." And the text [of the Gemara] did not see fit to explain and elaborate here why he would do [so].

Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:1:1.hebrew: מיתיבי התינוקות של בית רבן מסדרין פרשיותיהן כו' - אומר הר"ם: לפי' הקונטרס שפי' במתני' "החזן רואה היכן התינוקות קורין" לאור הנר — הא דלא פריך ליה ממתני' משום דאיכא למימר דקורין באיסור, ואין מוחין בידם; אבל הכא, דקתני "מסדרין", משמע שמותרין לעשות כן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:1:1.english: [The Gemara] raises an objection: "The schoolchildren arrange their sections, etc." - The Ram says: According to the explanation of the Kunteres [Rashi], who explained that in the Mishnah, "The attendant sees where the children are reading" [refers to reading] by the light of the lamp — the reason [the Gemara] did not object to him from the Mishnah is because one could say that they are reading in violation of the prohibition, and no one protests against them; but here, where it teaches "they arrange," it implies that they are permitted to do so.

Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:3:1.hebrew: רבא אמר רוב עם הארץ מעשרין הן - וא"ת: האמרי' בפרק בתרא דסוטה (דף מח.) שיוחנן כהן גדול גזר על הדמאי, לפי ששלח בכל גבול ישראל וראה שלא היו מפרישין אלא תרומה גדולה בלבד? וי"ל, דה"ק: שלא היו מפרישין כולם אלא תרומה גדולה, אבל רובן היו מעשרים. והא דחשו הכא טפי למיעוט מבמקום אחר — משום דהויא מיעוט דשכיח טובא, והיו הרבה נכשלים. ומה שקשה דאביי אדאביי ודרבא אדרבא — מפורש בפ"ב דכתובות (דף כד. ושם), גבי "חיישינן לגומלים":
Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:3:1.english: Rava said: Most amei ha'aretz tithe - And if you should say: But didn't we say in the last chapter of Sotah (48a) that Yochanan the High Priest decreed concerning demai [doubtfully tithed produce], because he sent [inspectors] throughout all the borders of Israel and saw that they were separating only terumah gedolah alone? And one can say that this is what it means: Not all of them were separating [tithes, but rather separated] only terumah gedolah, but most of them were tithing. And as for [the fact] that they were concerned here for the minority more than in other places — [it is] because it was a very common minority, and many were stumbling [into sin]. And as for what is difficult regarding [the apparent contradiction of] Abaye against Abaye and Rava against Rava, it is explained in the second chapter of Ketubot (24a and there), regarding "we are concerned for reciprocators" [chayshinan legomlim].

Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:8:1.hebrew: מה אשת רעהו הוא בבגדו והיא בבגדה אסור - והתם סברא הוא לאסור, לפי שיצרו תוקפו ומתגבר עליו ביותר. ורש"י פי': אפי' ביחוד נמי אסור מדאורייתא. ואין נראה, דמשמע דרוצה לאסור יחוד בנדה. תימה: דיחוד, דאסור מן התורה, לא ילפי' מאשת איש, ושרי בנדה כדכתיב "סוגה בשושנים" (סנהד' פ"ד לז.); והוא בבגדו והיא בבגדה, דלא הוי אפי' באשת איש אלא מדרבנן, אסור בנדה מהיקשא?! טפי הוה לן למיסר יחוד מהיקשא, ולמישרי הוא בבגדו והיא בבגדה בלא יחוד — כגון שפתח פתוח לרה"ר — מסוגה בשושנים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:8:1.english: “Just as with his neighbor’s wife, he in his clothes and she in her clothes is forbidden” - And there [in the case of a neighbor’s wife], it is logical reasoning to forbid [it], because his inclination overpowers him and overcomes him greatly. And Rashi explained that even [mere] seclusion is also forbidden from the Torah. But this does not appear [correct], as it implies that [the juxtaposition] seeks to forbid seclusion with a menstruating woman [niddah]. [And this is] astonishing: for seclusion, which is forbidden from the Torah [with a married woman], we do not derive from a married woman, and [rather] it is permitted with a niddah, as it is written: “hedged about with lilies” (Sanhedrin 37a); whereas [sleeping when] he is in his clothes and she is in her clothes, which even with a married woman is only Rabbinic, is forbidden with a niddah from the juxtaposition?! It would have been more [logical] for us to forbid seclusion from the juxtaposition, and to permit [sleeping when] he is in his clothes and she is in her clothes without seclusion — such as where the door is open to the public domain — based on “hedged about with lilies”!

Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:9:1.hebrew: ופליגא דר' פדת דא"ר פדת לא אסרה תורה אלא כו' - תימה: מנא ליה דפליגי? דילמא מדרבנן אסור, אפי' הוא בבגדו! ורש"י דפירש כאן: כיון דמדאורייתא לא אסור אלא תשמיש ממש, מדרבנן לא אסור אלא קירוב בשר — לא נהירא: דמסתמא לא פליגי אמתני' דלא יאכל הזב עם הזבה; ועוד, וכי לית ליה דאשת רעהו הוא בבגדו והיא בבגדה אסור?! ומפרש ר"ת: "ופליגא דר' פדת" — דכיון דלא אסרה תורה אלא קריבה של גילוי עריות בלבד, א"כ אין לנו לאסור ולגזור אלא כעין שאסר הכתוב, דהיינו דיעות בלא שינוי, כגון לא יאכל הזב עם הזבה; אבל הוא בבגדו והיא בבגדה, דאיכא דיעות ושינוי — לא; יסבור ר' פדת דאפי' באשת איש, הוא בבגדו והיא בבגדה שרי. ור"י פי': "ופליגא דר' פדת" — כיון דאית ליה דלא שייך לשון קריבה אלא בגילוי עריות ממש, וא"כ "ואל אשה נדה לא יקרב" היינו תשמיש ממש, שוב אין ללמוד בהיקש מאשת איש לאסור הוא בבגדו כו', לאפוקי לשון קריבה ממשמעותו. ודוחק הוא, דהא "אשת רעהו לא טמא" משמע תשמיש ממש, ואפילו הכי אסרי' הוא בבגדו והיא בבגדה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 13a:9:1.english: "And it disagrees with Rabbi Pedat, for Rabbi Pedat said: The Torah only prohibited etc." - It is astonishing: From where does [the Gemara] know that they disagree? Perhaps by Rabbinic law it is forbidden, even [when] he is in his clothes [and she is in her clothes]! And Rashi, who explained here: "Since by Torah law only actual intercourse is forbidden, by Rabbinic law only physical intimacy [touching of flesh] is forbidden" — [this] is not clear: for presumably they do not disagree with our Mishnah that "A zav may not eat with a zavah"; and furthermore, does he not maintain that with another man's wife, [sleeping together when] he is in his clothes and she is in her clothes is forbidden?! And Rabbeinu Tam explains [the statement], "And it disagrees with Rabbi Pedat": Since the Torah only prohibited proximity of illicit sexual relations alone, if so, we should not prohibit and decree [Rabbinically] except in a manner similar to what Scripture prohibited, which is [a situation with separate] minds without an unusual change [from the norm], such as "A zav may not eat with a zavah"; but [when] he is in his clothes and she is in her clothes, where there are [both separate] minds and an unusual change — no [we do not decree]; [and thus] Rabbi Pedat holds that even with a married woman, [sleeping together when] he is in his clothes and she is in her clothes is permitted. And the Ri explained [the statement], "And it disagrees with Rabbi Pedat": Since he maintains that the term "approach" [kerivah] only applies to actual illicit sexual relations, and if so, "And to a woman in her impurity you shall not approach" means actual intercourse, one can no longer learn through juxtaposition to another man's wife to prohibit [clothed sleeping where] he is in his clothes, etc., [which would] remove the term "approach" from its [literal] meaning. And this is difficult, for "neither has he defiled his neighbor's wife" [also] implies actual intercourse, and nevertheless we prohibit [when] he is in his clothes and she is in her clothes.
